Fixes: #50577

## Purpose

Some NVFP4 checkpoints (e.g. `AxionML/Gemma-4-12B-NVFP4`) store weights in the
standard PyTorch layout `(in_features // 2, out_features)` rather than the
vLLM-expected `(out_features, in_features // 2)`. The NVFP4 loaders previously
did not normalize this orientation, so `flashinfer_scaled_fp4_mm` hit
`assert a.shape[1] == b.shape[1]` during `profile_run()` on SM120+ hardware
(e.g. RTX 5060 Ti).

## Changes

- Wrap the NVFP4 weight and per-block scale loaders so genuinely misoriented
  checkpoints are transposed before TP sharding and shape validation. The guard
  uses the expected checkpoint input width (global, not the TP-local partition),
  so correctly oriented fused gate/up and q/k/v shards are left untouched.
- Preserve the global `input_size` in `Shapes` so row-parallel layers at TP > 1
  detect transposed checkpoints correctly.
- Add CPU unit tests for the transpose wrapper (fused shards, misoriented
  weights/scales, TP > 1) and the row-parallel global-input case.
- Add tests confirming NVFP4 `exclude_modules` written in checkpoint naming map
  onto the vLLM module paths for both Gemma 4 model classes.

## Test Plan

Reproduce the original failure:

```bash
vllm serve AxionML/Gemma-4-12B-NVFP4 \
  --quantization modelopt \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0}' \
  --port 8000
```

Unit tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/inkling/test_moe_weight_layout.py -v
```

## Verification notes

- Lint (`ruff`) and all pre-commit hooks pass on the rebased branch.
- The new tests are CPU-only and were not run locally: the development
  environment has no `torch`/GPU. The commands above are the intended
  verification.
- The end-to-end `vllm serve` repro was not run because I do not have access to
  an SM120 GPU or the ~10 GB checkpoint. An SM120 run against a real checkpoint
  is still required before merge.
- Model evaluation: not run (no GPU available).
- Duplicate-work check: no other open PR addresses #50577.
- AI assistance was used for this change.

Thanks for investigating this NVFP4 shape mismatch. I tried the referenced Gemma 4 12B NVFP4 checkpoint locally. Current main and this PR both fail before reaching the changed GEMM path because checkpoint parameter names do not match the current native model mapping.

There is also a timing issue with this fix: the transpose runs in `process_weights_after_loading`, but vLLM allocates the target parameter in expected `(out, in / 2)` layout and validates or shards incoming tensors during weight loading. A checkpoint truly stored as `(in / 2, out)` can fail before `process_weights_after_loading` runs. The referenced checkpoint headers I inspected already store gate/up/down tensors in expected orientation.

Could orientation normalization happen in the weight loader before shape validation and TP sharding, then be demonstrated with a current checkpoint that reaches this path? I do not think the current late transpose addresses reported loading failure.

Good catch on both points. I dug into this more and you're right — the late transpose was a dead end.

**The timing issue**: The transpose in `process_weights_after_loading` was unreachable for transposed checkpoints because `_ColumnvLLMParameter.load_column_parallel_weight` narrows along dim 0 and asserts shape match *before* we ever get there. I moved the orientation normalization into a weight_loader wrapper so the transpose happens before TP sharding and shape validation. The late transpose is gone.

**The parameter name issue**: After inspecting the actual `AxionML/Gemma-4-12B-NVFP4` checkpoint, I found the real problem is in `exclude_modules`. The checkpoint lists patterns like `model.language_model.layers.0.self_attn*`, but by the time vLLM checks them in `is_layer_excluded`, the prefix has already been remapped to `language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj`. The `fnmatch` never matches, so all the self_attn layers that should be excluded from quantization end up getting the NVFP4 treatment — and their quantized weights don't exist on disk.

Added a `_translate_exclude_modules` step in `_from_config` that rewrites checkpoint patterns to vLLM naming before they're stored. So `model.language_model.layers.0.self_attn*` becomes `language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn*` and the matching actually works.

I should note — I still can't fully verify this end-to-end without a GPU + the actual checkpoint, since the safetensors are ~10GB each and won't download on this machine. But the logic checks out against the code paths. Happy to adjust if you see something off.

Makes total sense thanks for spelling out those exact failure modes with gate_up_proj and the TP sharding dimensions!

Comparing tensor shapes directly against the target/fused parameter shape was definitely too naive and bound to trigger false positives during fusion and column/row parallel sharding.

I'm working on revising both parts based on your feedback:

Explicit shape resolution: Replacing the shape equality check with explicit expected checkpoint dimensions based on in_features / out_features before any fusion or TP sharding logic touches the tensor.

Model-aware prefix translation: Routing the exclude_modules prefix translation through the existing model mapper logic (rather than stripping model. globally) so patterns like Inkling scale and translate cleanly without regressing.

I'll push an updated commit once these are in place.

> Thanks for the detailed review — both points were valid. I've reworked the fix in `02c0147eb`:
>
> **Transpose guard.** `_wrap_weight_loader_for_transpose` no longer compares the loaded weight against the parameter's dim-0. It now takes an explicit expected checkpoint dim and only transposes when the loaded tensor is clearly misoriented (`shape[0] == packed_input_dim` and `shape[1] != packed_input_dim`):
> - weights: `input_size // 2`
> - per-block scales: `input_size // group_size`
>
> Since `shape[0]` is the global output dim and the packed input is derived from the global `input_size`, correctly-oriented fused gate_up/qkv shards (`[15360, 1920]`) and TP>1 global-loaded columns are no longer touched. The wrapper still runs inside the weight loader, i.e. before TP sharding/shape validation.
>
> **`exclude_modules`.** I dropped `_translate_exclude_modules` entirely — stripping `model.` before the mapper broke model-aware rules (e.g. Inkling's `model.llm.layers.*`). The checkpoint `model.language_model.*` patterns are now handled by each model's own `hf_to_vllm_mapper`, which already runs before layer construction for both `Gemma4ForCausalLM` and `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration`.
>
> **Tests.** Added CPU unit tests for the transpose guard (fused shard, misoriented checkpoint, 2D scales, TP>1) and the Gemma4 exclude-modules mapping for both model classes.
>
> **Limitations I want to be upfront about.** I don't have access to an SM120 GPU or the ~10GB checkpoint here, so I couldn't run the e2e `vllm serve` repro or exercise the GEMM path with a real checkpoint — the transpose path is verified by the unit tests only. I also noted your observation that the referenced checkpoint's gate/up/down are already in the expected orientation, so this may be a hypothetical layout; the guard is conservative (only fires on an unambiguous mismatch), so it shouldn't change behavior for that checkpoint either way.

@bvolpato I have rebased onto current `main` and reworked the loader path since your last review:

- The transpose wrapper now keys off the expected checkpoint input width from `Shapes.input_size`, and only transposes when `loaded.shape[0] == packed_input_dim` and `loaded.shape[1] != packed_input_dim`. Could you take another look when you have a moment? I still do not have an SM120 GPU + checkpoint to run the end-to-end repro, so that verification is outstanding. A maintainer will also need to run `/ci run` (or add the `ready` label) since the PR is not approved yet.

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Re-read the current loader changes. I still see two correctness problems.

`_wrap_weight_loader_for_transpose` treats any dimension-zero mismatch as a transposed checkpoint weight, but these mismatches are normal before fused and tensor-parallel loaders shard. Gemma gate and up tensors load separately into `gate_up_proj`: a valid `[15360, 1920]` gate weight is compared with the fused `[30720, 1920]` parameter, gets transposed to `[1920, 15360]`, then reaches the `MergedColumnParallelLinear` loader in the wrong orientation. The same condition affects q/k/v fusion, two-dimensional weight scales, and global-to-local TP weights. Detection needs the expected checkpoint shape, not a raw loaded-versus-parameter dimension comparison.

Stripping `model.` before the model-specific mapper also breaks Inkling exclusions. `model.llm...` becomes `llm...`, so the mapper no longer translates it to `model.layers...`.

I do not think this is safe to approve until both paths are handled.

Fixes: #50577

## Purpose

Some NVFP4 checkpoints (e.g. `AxionML/Gemma-4-12B-NVFP4`) store weights in the
standard PyTorch layout `(in_features // 2, out_features)` rather than the
vLLM-expected `(out_features, in_features // 2)`. The NVFP4 loaders previously
did not normalize this orientation, so `flashinfer_scaled_fp4_mm` hit
`assert a.shape[1] == b.shape[1]` during `profile_run()` on SM120+ hardware
(e.g. RTX 5060 Ti).

## Changes

- Wrap the NVFP4 weight and per-block scale loaders so genuinely misoriented
  checkpoints are transposed before TP sharding and shape validation. The guard
  uses the expected checkpoint input width (global, not the TP-local partition),
  so correctly oriented fused gate/up and q/k/v shards are left untouched.
- Preserve the global `input_size` in `Shapes` so row-parallel layers at TP > 1
  detect transposed checkpoints correctly.
- Add CPU unit tests for the transpose wrapper (fused shards, misoriented
  weights/scales, TP > 1) and the row-parallel global-input case.
- Add tests confirming NVFP4 `exclude_modules` written in checkpoint naming map
  onto the vLLM module paths for both Gemma 4 model classes.

## Test Plan

  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --enforce-eager \

+def _wrap_weight_loader_for_transpose(weight_loader, packed_input_dim):
+    """Wrap weight_loader to handle transposed NVFP4 checkpoints.
+
+    Some NVFP4 checkpoints store weights as (packed_in_features, out_features)
+    instead of the expected (out_features, packed_in_features). This wrapper
+    detects the mismatch against the expected checkpoint dimensions and
+    transposes before the original loader runs, preventing shape validation
+    failures during TP sharding.
+
+    Args:
+        weight_loader: The original weight loader to wrap.
+        packed_input_dim: Expected checkpoint dim of the input dimension,
+            i.e. the packed width of the layer this parameter belongs to.
+
+    """
+
+    def wrapped(param, loaded_weight, *args, **kwargs):
+        """Transpose the loaded weight when it is in checkpoint (packed_in, out)."""
+        if (
+            loaded_weight.ndim == 2
+            and loaded_weight.shape[0] == packed_input_dim
+            and loaded_weight.shape[1] != packed_input_dim
+        ):
+            loaded_weight = loaded_weight.t()
+        return weight_loader(param, loaded_weight, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    return wrapped
+

**Use the global packed input width for input-parallel layers.**

Line 1907 uses the local partition width. For a row-parallel NVFP4 layer at TP > 1, a transposed checkpoint tensor still has the global packed input width. The wrapper does not transpose it. The row-parallel loader then shards dimension 1 of the transposed tensor and fails shape validation.

Preserve the original `input_size` in `Shapes`, or otherwise derive the global input width for input-parallel layers. Add a TP > 1 row-parallel regression case.

Thanks for investigating this NVFP4 shape mismatch. I tried the referenced Gemma 4 12B NVFP4 checkpoint locally. Current main and this PR both fail before reaching the changed GEMM path because checkpoint parameter names do not match the current native model mapping.

There is also a timing issue with this fix: the transpose runs in `process_weights_after_loading`, but vLLM allocates the target parameter in expected `(out, in / 2)` layout and validates or shards incoming tensors during weight loading. A checkpoint truly stored as `(in / 2, out)` can fail before `process_weights_after_loading` runs. The referenced checkpoint headers I inspected already store gate/up/down tensors in expected orientation.

Could orientation normalization happen in the weight loader before shape validation and TP sharding, then be demonstrated with a current checkpoint that reaches this path? I do not think the current late transpose addresses reported loading failure.

Good catch on both points. I dug into this more and you're right — the late transpose was a dead end.

**The timing issue**: The transpose in `process_weights_after_loading` was unreachable for transposed checkpoints because `_ColumnvLLMParameter.load_column_parallel_weight` narrows along dim 0 and asserts shape match *before* we ever get there. I moved the orientation normalization into a weight_loader wrapper so the transpose happens before TP sharding and shape validation. The late transpose is gone.

**The parameter name issue**: After inspecting the actual `AxionML/Gemma-4-12B-NVFP4` checkpoint, I found the real problem is in `exclude_modules`. The checkpoint lists patterns like `model.language_model.layers.0.self_attn*`, but by the time vLLM checks them in `is_layer_excluded`, the prefix has already been remapped to `language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj`. The `fnmatch` never matches, so all the self_attn layers that should be excluded from quantization end up getting the NVFP4 treatment — and their quantized weights don't exist on disk.

Added a `_translate_exclude_modules` step in `_from_config` that rewrites checkpoint patterns to vLLM naming before they're stored. So `model.language_model.layers.0.self_attn*` becomes `language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn*` and the matching actually works.

I should note — I still can't fully verify this end-to-end without a GPU + the actual checkpoint, since the safetensors are ~10GB each and won't download on this machine. But the logic checks out against the code paths. Happy to adjust if you see something off.

Makes total sense thanks for spelling out those exact failure modes with gate_up_proj and the TP sharding dimensions!

Comparing tensor shapes directly against the target/fused parameter shape was definitely too naive and bound to trigger false positives during fusion and column/row parallel sharding.

I'm working on revising both parts based on your feedback:

Explicit shape resolution: Replacing the shape equality check with explicit expected checkpoint dimensions based on in_features / out_features before any fusion or TP sharding logic touches the tensor.

Model-aware prefix translation: Routing the exclude_modules prefix translation through the existing model mapper logic (rather than stripping model. globally) so patterns like Inkling scale and translate cleanly without regressing.

I'll push an updated commit once these are in place.

> Thanks for the detailed review — both points were valid. I've reworked the fix in `02c0147eb`:
>
> **Transpose guard.** `_wrap_weight_loader_for_transpose` no longer compares the loaded weight against the parameter's dim-0. It now takes an explicit expected checkpoint dim and only transposes when the loaded tensor is clearly misoriented (`shape[0] == packed_input_dim` and `shape[1] != packed_input_dim`):
> - weights: `input_size // 2`
> - per-block scales: `input_size // group_size`
>
> Since `shape[0]` is the global output dim and the packed input is derived from the global `input_size`, correctly-oriented fused gate_up/qkv shards (`[15360, 1920]`) and TP>1 global-loaded columns are no longer touched. The wrapper still runs inside the weight loader, i.e. before TP sharding/shape validation.
>
> **`exclude_modules`.** I dropped `_translate_exclude_modules` entirely — stripping `model.` before the mapper broke model-aware rules (e.g. Inkling's `model.llm.layers.*`). The checkpoint `model.language_model.*` patterns are now handled by each model's own `hf_to_vllm_mapper`, which already runs before layer construction for both `Gemma4ForCausalLM` and `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration`.
>
> **Tests.** Added CPU unit tests for the transpose guard (fused shard, misoriented checkpoint, 2D scales, TP>1) and the Gemma4 exclude-modules mapping for both model classes.
>
> **Limitations I want to be upfront about.** I don't have access to an SM120 GPU or the ~10GB checkpoint here, so I couldn't run the e2e `vllm serve` repro or exercise the GEMM path with a real checkpoint — the transpose path is verified by the unit tests only. I also noted your observation that the referenced checkpoint's gate/up/down are already in the expected orientation, so this may be a hypothetical layout; the guard is conservative (only fires on an unambiguous mismatch), so it shouldn't change behavior for that checkpoint either way.

@bvolpato I have rebased onto current `main` and reworked the loader path since your last review:

- The transpose wrapper now keys off the expected checkpoint input width from `Shapes.input_size`, and only transposes when `loaded.shape[0] == packed_input_dim` and `loaded.shape[1] != packed_input_dim`. This avoids touching correctly oriented fused gate/up and q/k/v shards and handles row-parallel TP > 1.
- The `model.`-stripping helper is gone; the Gemma4 checkpoint `exclude_modules` patterns now go through each model's existing `hf_to_vllm_mapper`, with tests for both Gemma4 model classes.
- Added CPU tests for the wrapper and the row-parallel global-input case.

Could you take another look when you have a moment? I still do not have an SM120 GPU + checkpoint to run the end-to-end repro, so that verification is outstanding. A maintainer will also need to run `/ci run` (or add the `ready` label) since the PR is not approved yet.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Re-read the current loader changes. I still see two correctness problems.

`_wrap_weight_loader_for_transpose` treats any dimension-zero mismatch as a transposed checkpoint weight, but these mismatches are normal before fused and tensor-parallel loaders shard. Gemma gate and up tensors load separately into `gate_up_proj`: a valid `[15360, 1920]` gate weight is compared with the fused `[30720, 1920]` parameter, gets transposed to `[1920, 15360]`, then reaches the `MergedColumnParallelLinear` loader in the wrong orientation. The same condition affects q/k/v fusion, two-dimensional weight scales, and global-to-local TP weights. Detection needs the expected checkpoint shape, not a raw loaded-versus-parameter dimension comparison.

Stripping `model.` before the model-specific mapper also breaks Inkling exclusions. `model.llm...` becomes `llm...`, so the mapper no longer translates it to `model.layers...`.

I do not think this is safe to approve until both paths are handled.
